note: Triennial election of the 23 district electoral divisions of Ballymena rural district, one member each (Belfast News-Letter, 9 May 1924). Polling in the four contested divisions (Ahoghill, Ballyscullion, Galgorm and Kirkinriola) took place on Thursday 5 June 1924 and the results were declared on 6 June. Eighteen divisions were returned unopposed, several after withdrawals (Ballymena Observer, 9 and 16 May 1924, p. 10). Glenbuck had no nomination; the new council co-opted Samuel Shaw as its member on 10 June 1924 (Ballymena Observer, 13 June 1924, p. 6), which is not an election and is not recorded as a result. Sole nomination; sitting member. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of the Ballymena Observer, 16 May 1924, p. 10 (council-audit, Nov 2026): Samuel M'Miller is printed Samuel M'Millen, the sitting member (M'Millen again in 1930). Renamed from 'Tullygrawley' to Tullaghgarley (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1925-69 name the DED Tullaghgarley; the rounds were filed as Tullygrawley (1924); Tullygarley (1927, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964); Tullaghgarley (1967). This round was filed as 'Tullygrawley', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (tullygrawley) answers with a redirect to this one.
